summary.en: U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth arrived in Bogotá, delivered a C-130 and met with President De la Espriella to deepen security cooperation, while also announcing a US-Venezuela military partnership in Caracas. Colombia rejected a U.S. proposal for joint anti-drug strikes and De la Espriella ordered a tenth bombing against a narcoterrorist target in Valle del Cauca. In Kyiv, a 19‑year-old woman was detained for poisoning a former Colombian soldier of the Ukrainian Armed Forces for $1,000. The conflict recorded 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
